Three. Xe has 8 valence electrons, 2 go into bonds, and 6 remain.

s: 1 atm is below the **triple-point pressure**, 5.11 atm.
Below it, liquid CO₂ cannot exist.
Only solid or gas is possible.
298 K is far above the sublimation temperature, so gas.
t: A supercritical fluid needs more than 73 atm and more than 304 K.
Solid and liquid meet only at or above the triple-point pressure of 5.11 atm.
Solid CO₂ at 1 atm needs about 195 K. At 298 K it has sublimed.
Liquid CO₂ needs at least 5.11 atm. At 1 atm it never forms.
c: Why does dry ice sublime instead of melting on a table?
Room pressure, 1 atm, is below the triple-point pressure, so the liquid is never stable.

c: What is the hybridization of S in SF₄?

s: No concentration appears in that formula.

A zero-order half-life is [A]₀/(2k), so it grows with the starting concentration.
c: A zero-order reaction starts with twice as much A. What happens to its half-life?
It doubles.

s: ΔH is favorable, ΔS is not, so it runs below 800 K.
t: This slips a power of ten. Convert kJ to J first: 120,000 / 150 = 800.
Spontaneous at all temperatures needs a negative ΔH with a positive ΔS. Here ΔS is negative.
This reads the 120 from ΔH as a temperature. Divide ΔH by ΔS.
Above 800 K the unfavorable entropy term wins. This reaction is spontaneous below it.
c: With ΔH positive and ΔS positive, when is a reaction spontaneous?
Above the crossover temperature, where the entropy term wins.
